newsitem.title: USA: CBOT head sees opportunity, risks for U.S. grain.
newsitem.headline: CBOT head sees opportunity, risks for U.S. grain.

text.p: Chicago Board of Trade chairman Patrick Arbor said the U.S. grains industry faces great risks and opportunities as a result of the government's revamped agricultural policy implemented last year by Congress.

"The Freedom to Farm bill is certainly a great opportunity to us all, but it also presents great risks," Arbor told grain industry leaders attending the annual convention of the National Grain and Feed Association.

Arbor said that as farmers have greater flexibility in planting and marketing decisions due to significantly less government intervention, producers and the industry also need to develop new tools in risk managment and said the CBOT "stands ready to help."

A significant change the CBOT appears ready to approve is a major overhaul of its delivery system for corn and soybean futures contracts. Arbor said there will be a full membership meeting on the proposed new delivery system on April 1 and that a vote is scheduled for April 15.

The new system would establish delivery points along the northern Illinois River from Chicago to Pekin, Ill. and Burn Harbor, Ind. Toledo and St. Louis would be deleted as approved delivery locations.
The National Grain and Feed Association has been strongly in favor of changing the current delivery system.
Arbor urged the industry to support the proposal, which is open for public comment to the Commodity Futures Trading Commission through March 31.
